chapter_title: Concerning the Body: It was constructed after the
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the K ephalaia Chapter

---

** ¶2:**

The whole spiritual world, from its in most celest ial degree to its outermost natural degree , is ordered according to the form of the Grand Human; and the formation of the individual human mind , in all its fac ulties, acc ords to the form of the spiritual world entire .

---

**¶3:** The in most rational faculty is like the first and highest expression of the five degrees of truth that clothe interior wisdom. From the first descent below the in most, down to the seat of the will , the mind is arranged according to ten distinct degrees of heav enly order. The will itself acc ords to the ever -turning cycle through which the Lord 's life flows in perpet ual infl ux. From the will down ward to the fac ulties that process and ass imilate spiritual nourishment, the mind resemb les that intermediate realm of spiritual states extending between the higher heav ens and the natural degree . The gener ative natural faculty corresponds to the great plane of out ward life . From the organs of spiritual ass imilation down to the supports of out ward conduct , the mind is arranged according to three degrees of the natural mind . The lower supports of the spiritual structure correspond to the space in which the sust aining power of the ou termost degree holds its ground . The outermost natural foundation corresponds to the great plane upon which that sustaining power stands, together with the four bonds that anchor it below . The organ of interior purification corresponds to the containing form of self-love. The self hood in its prop rium corresponds to the containing form of fals ity. The living truth cours ing through every faculty corresponds to the containing form of natural truth.

---

**¶4 :** In this way the individual mind corresponds to the whole spiritual world — in its heav enly degrees, its ord erings, its elevated states of perception , its boundaries of protection , and its containing forms of aff ection, as has now been made plain .

---

**¶5:**

There exist five great provinces of spiritual governance in the ou termost region of the spiritual world, over each of which one of the five ruling principles of the Lord's sust aining power pres ides.

---

**¶6:**

In the first and highest degree of spiritual guardianship, where the Principle of Celest ial Rad iance gov erns, upon the summit of all the works of creation , its domin ion extends over the three in most heavens. Those beneath it serve under the Principle of Honor and Spiritual Glory .

---

**¶7 :** The second degree of guard ianship, where the Principle of Spiritual Glory governs, extends its dominion over the seven degrees of heav enly arrangement that lie beneath it.

---

** ¶8:** The third degree of guardianship, where the Principle of Imm ovable Truth governs, reigns from the lower heavens down to the natural degree of the mind. It viv ifies, according to its authority , the turning cycle of infl ux, the intermediate spiritual states, and the four modes of natural life that are established in the ou termost degree .

---

**¶9 :** The fourth degree of guardian ship, where the Principle of the Lord 's Divine Power governs, pres ides over the three tur nings of the cycle . Its authority extends over the three planes of the natural mind that rest upon the sust aining power at the foundation .

---

**¶10:**

The fifth degree of guardianship is that in which the Sust aining Power of the ou termost degree holds authority . It gov erns the great plane of natural life upon which it stands, and the four anch oring bonds beneath it.

---

**¶ 11:** Spiritual crisis and temptation have ar isen in each of these five degrees of guardianship from age to age.

---

** ¶12:** In the province of Celestial Radiance, the evil of self -love desired to project itself up ward toward the image of Divine Truth made visible . Yet it was barred from that place and fell back into its own shame.

---

**¶ 13:** In the province of Spiritual Glory, a great uph eaval and betray al occurred, in which the guardian aff ections that had risen up at that time — those who had been sent — descended from their station until they were brought low and humbled.

---

** ¶14:** In the province of Immovable Truth, the m isb eg otten forms of fals ity descended into the natural degree and fashioned the figure of the fleshly self hood — the proprium in its corpor eal form.

---

** ¶15:** In the province of the Lord 's Divine Power, a commotion arose in the three planes of the natural mind above the sustaining foundation . The pathway was obstructed for the ascent of the three cycles of pur ification: that of rational perception , that of natural truth , and that of the will 's love .

---

**¶16 :** In the province of the Sust aining Power, the anch oring bonds beneath were exposed and st rained at their chains. A great spiritual conv ulsion sh ook that ou termost degree .

---

**¶23 :** The teaching of wisdom, which circulates through the whole mind , corresponds to the perception of truth born of innoc ence, which asc ends and descends through every degree of the spiritual world, from the highest to the lowest.

---

**¶24:** Love and joy, faith and truth — in which the regener ating person must live — correspond to the two great vessels of celest ial light : the vessel of good in the will and the vessel of truth in the understanding. For the living soul must ascend by means of these two, and be lib erated through them. Through good and truth it rises from the depths of the natural mind and arrives at the heights of the celest ial degree .

---

**¶25 :**

Understand this further : there exist four distinct real ms within the individual mind, and in each of these four real ms d well inn umerable dominant affections, seven times multipl ied.

---

**¶26:**

The first realm is the in most rational faculty, from the summit of the mind . The seven dominant affections that govern this highest realm are these : two belonging to interior sight — the perception of good and the perception of truth; two belonging to interior hearing — the reception of celest ial instruction and the reception of spiritual instruction ; two belonging to interior disc ernment of what is genuine — the discrimination of good from evil and truth from falsity. The seventh is the faculty of interior taste — the capacity to sa vor wisdom , which is the opening through which all spiritual n ourishment enters .

---

**¶27 :** The second realm extends from below the inmost faculty through the whole region of the understanding and the will . Its seven dominant affections are: two fac ulties of out ward action that correspond to the two organs of hearing in the realm above — for what is heard inter iorly is expressed outwardly through de eds; two aff ections of spiritual n ourishing that correspond to the organs of disc ernment above ; two interior eyes of the will — the will 's own perception of good and truth within the heart ; and the passage through which spiritual nourishment desc ends between them , which in this middle region corresponds to the faculty of interior taste in the realm above .

---

**¶28 :** In the third realm of the mind there exist seven dominant affections, which are : the aff ection of de light, the affection of spiritual resp iration, the affection of pur ification, the affection of interior self -love that must be subd ued, the affection of bitter z eal, and two affections of disc ernment that serve the lower natural mind .

---

**¶29 :** In the fourth and lowest realm, there are another seven of this same kind: two aff ections of outward support , two affections of gener ative power , two affections of bod ily strength , and the faculty through which interior truth issues forth into the ou termost natural degree, beg etting all the forms of life in the world .

---

**¶31 :** The twelve fundamental states of spiritual life — which are: the state of innoc ence and leadership , the state of natural good , the state of the marriage of good and truth, the state of external aff ection, the state of confidence and power , the state of interior disc ernment, the state of equilib rium and judgment , the state of spiritual crisis , the state of interior perception and elevation , the state of out ward ob edience, the state of truth serving good , and the state of ultim ates and completion — these are the twelve ordered states that exist in the heav ens above, upon the turning cycle of infl ux. They are interlocked and bound upon this perpet ually revol ving sphere of providence , in which they are fixed and impl anted. And regarding all these twelve fundamental states, this is how they were appointed and made to govern in ordered succession upon the turning cycle beneath the in most heaven. They are arranged so that one may find the beginning and the end, the first and the last, linked together in a circle .

---

**¶32 :** These same twelve states are found , one following another, within the individual mind. They are counted in order and degree from the in most to the outermost. The inmost rational faculty is Innoc ence. The conn ective faculty of understanding is Natural Good. The two arms of out ward action are the Marriage of Good and Truth. The region of the understanding is External Affection. The region of the interior will is Confidence and Power. The gener ative center is Interior Discernment. The central axis of order and the faculty of ass imilation are Equilibrium and Judgment. The faculty of propag ation is Spiritual Crisis. The supports of conduct are Interior Perception. The joints of humble obedience are Outward Obedience. The lower supports of the spiritual structure are Truth Serving Good. The outermost natural foundation is the state of Ultimates and Completion.

---

**¶33:**

These twelve states are also distributed in altern ation . They exist within the mind as if turned to face one another and bent into correspondence , after the pattern of the twelve spiritual states in the heavens. They too are thus arranged, one against another, beginning joined to end, as they occur upon the revol ving cycle of providence .

---

**¶34 :** They are also counted by order and degree throughout the whole mind and all its fac ulties. They are turned to face one another, bent, and spread throughout ; for from the inmost faculty down to the center , six are counted to one side, and another six to the other side.

---

**¶35:**

The six that belong to the side of good — the right — are these: the right aspect of the inmost rational faculty is Innoc ence; the right support of understanding is Natural Good; the right arm of outward action is the Marriage of Good and Truth; the right enc losure of the will is External Affection; the interior of the will is Confidence and Power; and the right aspect of the generative faculty is Interior Discernment.

---

**¶36:**

Conversely, the other six, which belong to the side of truth — the left — come in the opposite direction, from the center back up to the inmost: the left aspect of the lower faculty is Equilib rium; the left enc losure of the understanding is Spiritual Crisis; the left aff ection of n ourishing and the left organ of discernment are Interior Perception; the left joint of action is Outward Obedience ; the left support of understanding is Truth Serving Good; the left aspect of the in most rational faculty is Ultim ates and Completion. This is how the divine order itself has arranged them. It has set them in correspondence , one facing its companion, beginning joined to end — so that good and truth face one another throughout the whole form of the regener ating mind .

---

**¶38 :** There exist inn umerable powers within the individual mind. They are the aff ections and thoughts that dwell within it as inhabitants of their own houses . Countless my riads of ruling aff ections are established throughout the human mind . They are distributed and fixed , quartered each according to its own containing form . The number of their containing forms — the discrete vessels of aff ection and thought — is beyond r eckoning.

---

** ¶39:** When all these ruling affections st ir and move within the mind, they encounter one another; and they ass ail and destroy one another, and produce conflict within . When at last the ev ils e rupt from the mind of the person who is under going spiritual death , they produce painful inflamm ations of self -love, eru ptions of fals ity, and burning wounds of evil desire throughout the mind . Either they may have corru pted the person within, in the interior will ; or else they may break forth upon the exterior life for all to see. These eru ptions of evil must first be pressed upon through tem ptation and discharge their fals ity, and empty out their corruption , until the interior evil is thoroughly pressed out and the put ref action forced from the wound. Afterward , the mind closes over and heals; and the person obt ains relief from the spiritual diseases that had surf aced — for what was hidden within has now been brought forth , pur ged , and made whole.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: This whole universe, above and below, reflects the pattern of the human body; as the formation of this body of flesh accords to the pattern of the universe.

Its head is like the first-fruits of the five garments. And, from its neck down to the site of its heart, it resembles the pattern of the ten firmaments. And again, the heart accords to the wheel of the rotating sphere. And, from its heart down to its intestines (?), is like this atmosphere that extends from the sphere down to the earth. The [male] part of the body corresponds to this great earth. And also, from its intestines (?) down to its loins is like the three earths. And also, its shinbones to the pattern of the space in which the Porter stands. Its footsoles to the great earth upon which the Porter is stood; and the four fastenings that are under his feet. Its liver to the vessel of fire. Its flesh to the vessel of darkness. Its blood to the vessel of water.
Now, this is how the small body corresponds to the macro-cosmos in its firmaments, in its orderings, in its mountains, its walls and its vessels.
There exist five great camps in this great outer zone, of which the five sons of the Living Spirit are masters.

So, in the first watch-station above, of which the Keeper of Splendour is master, on the battlement of all the works, is found his authority over the three heavens. Then the ones below him [serve under the watch of] the great King of Honour.
The second watch, of which the great King of Honour is master, his own authority (extends) over the seven firmaments beneath him.

The third watch, of which the Adamant [is master, his authority] reigns from the firmament down below to the [earth]. [And he] invigorates, according to his authority, the sphere and the worlds of the atmosphere; and the other four worlds that are appointed on this earth.
The fourth watch, over which the King of Glory has power, is the three wheels. And his authority lies over the three earths upon the head of the Porter.
The fifth watch is the watch over which the Porter is authoritative. Again, he is master, according to his authority, over this great earth he stands upon, and the four fastenings under his feet.
Affliction has come about in these five watches from time to time.
So, in the watch of the Keeper of Splendour, Sin desired to spurt up towards the image of the Ambassador. Yet, they barred it from that place, and it fell back down in shame.

Again, an earthquake and treachery occurred in the watch of the great King of Honour, which the watchers who had arisen at the time and had [abandoned their watch —] they who were sent came down, until they were humbled.
Also, in the watch of the Adamant, the abortions came to the earth and fashioned [the] figure of flesh.

Again, in the watch of the King of Glory, a commotion happened in these three earths above the Porter. The pathway was obstructed for the ascent of these three wheels; that of wind, that of water, and that of fire.
Also, in the watch of the Porter, the fastenings beneath were laid bare and strained their chains. A great earthquake befell that place.

[Like] these five watch-stations, which exist in this great [outer zone, with these five] camps: this is also the case with this body. There are another five camps there, and the Light Mind is watching over them, and the new man who is with him.
Also, the teaching of wisdom, which circulates in that body: to the likeness of the Virgin of Light, who goes up and comes down in this zone, above and below.

Also, love and joy, faith and truth: they are to the likeness of these two light ships. For, the living soul should go up in them and become free through them; and it ascends from the abysses below and arrives at the heights above.
There exist four worlds in this body of the flesh, and there exist countless times seven rulers in the body of the four worlds!

So, the first world is from its neck up; and also the seven rulers who are in this upper world are these: the two organs of sight, and the two of hearing, and the two of smell. The other one is the mouth, which is the organ of taste.

The second world is from its neck down to its entire upper torso. And also, the seven rulers who are in this second world are: its two arms that accord to the pattern of its two ears, which occur in its first world above; and its two breasts that are to the pattern of its organs of smell; and the two eyes of its heart; and the gullet of the stomach between the two breasts, which in the chest is the pattern of the mouth.
Once more, there exist seven rulers in the third world of the body, which are these: the fat, the lung, the spleen, the liver, the gall, and its two kidneys.

Also, the fourth world below. There are another seven there of this same kind: its two buttocks (?), and its two testicles, and its two loins; and the member out of which the seed comes, that begets all the forms.

Aries and Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces; these are the twelve signs of the zodiac that occur in the worlds above, on the sphere. They are interlocked and bound on this turning wheel, the one in which they are [fastened], fixed, and planted. And, regarding all these twelve signs of the zodiac, this is how they were appointed and made leaders [in their order] on the sphere beneath the heaven that is the wheel of the stars.

Again, they occur like this, these that we have recited, one after another in this body. They are counted by order and number from the head to the feet. Its head is Aries. Its neck and its shoulders are Taurus. Its two arms Gemini. Its upper torso is Cancer. Its stomach is Leo. Its belly is Virgo. The vertical spine and its intestines (?) are Libra. Its genitals Scorpio. Its loins are Sagittarius. Its knees are Capricorn. Its shinbones are Aquarius. The soles of its feet are Pisces.

Behold, these are also distributed one after another. They exist in this body, as if turned to the side and bent to the pattern of the twelve signs of the zodiac. They too are thus, arranged one against another, head to tail, as they occur on the wheel [from below] up.
Also, they are counted by order and number of the body and all its members. Because from its head down to its hip shall count six to its left, and another six to its right.

The six that are down its right are these that I will recount: the right temple is Aries; its right shoulder is Taurus; its right arm is Gemini; its right rib-cage is Cancer; its stomach is Leo; the right side of its reproductive organs are Virgo.

Conversely, the other six about which we have spoken, which are to its left, in contrast they come from its hip to its head: its left [hip] is Libra; its left rib-cage is Scorpio; its left breast and left kidney is Sagittarius; its [left] elbow is Capricorn; its left shoulder is Aquarius; its left temple is Pisces. This is how the creator of the body himself has appointed them. He has [set] them in order and arranged them, one against its companion, head to tail.

There exist many powers in this body. They are the house-dwellers who are made the leaders in it. There are eight hundred and forty times ten thousand rulers made chiefs in the human body! They are distributed and set firm, quartered according to house. The count and number of their houses is two hundred and ten times ten thousand.

When all these rulers come creeping and moving within the body, they will meet one another; and they shall beset and destroy one another, and [make war] in them there. When [at last] they shall erupt from the body of the person who [will] die; and make putrid boils and sores and burning wounds in the body. Either they might have made him sick within; or else they might come forth upon his outer side. Those wounds shall first be squeezed and discharge their liquid, and empty out their pus, until they are squeezed [dry and clean] and the suppuration forced out from the wound. Afterwards, their scars shall close over; and they are healed and obtain relief from the places that came out upon them.
